en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/ending/s0.l73.c13/text:
Order!

Richard M Nixon, how do you plead on 1 count of treason against the United States of America, 1 count of misappropriation of campaign funds, 1 count of obstruction of justice, one count of abuse of power, one count of…

Richard Nixon, as he heard all this droning from the judge, closed his eyes, waiting for the sentence to end. He had been up all night, unable to sleep due to all the stress from the trial. Before he knew it, he’d fallen unconscious. All of a sudden, he jolted awake to the sound of the judge screaming; "NIXON! What do you plead?..."

"Uh, not guilty, your honour… not guilty?"

"On 1 count of sleeping in a court of law?..."

"When did you say tha- actually yes, your honour. The liberal media has been painting an askew picture of me. I was merely resting my eyes."
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/ending/s0.l77.c14/text:
Hubert Humphrey's inauguration address, January 20th, 1969.

Today I have stood, where once Abraham Lincoln stood and took an oath to my country. It is very appropriate then that from this bastion of America, this very heart of the great men who created the principles of freedom in this country, that today we sound the drum for freedom as have our generations of forebears before us done, time and time again through history. Let us rise to the call of freedom-loving blood that is in us and send our answer to the tyranny that clanks its chains upon the Negro. In the name of the greatest country that has ever trod this earth, I draw the line in the dust and toss the gauntlet before the feet of tyranny . . . and I say . . . desegregation today . . . desegregation tomorrow . . . desegregation forever!
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/ending/s0.l93.c27/text: The murders and rioting in America will be your first order of business, and more long term, the war on Vietnam. If both of those are dealt with, your silent majority will be pleased. Other than that, inflation must be dealt with, as well as the excess of Great Society. Good luck, and welcome back to the executive branch!
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/ending/s0.l95.c32/text: Congratulations! Despite the intense battle from Humphrey and Wallace, you have disproven the doubters and redeemed your name. Your performance in debates and campaigning were widely praised compared to 1960, which allowed you to win with a massive landslide. What a turnaround from 1964!
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/ending/s0.l97.c32/text: Congratulations! Despite the intense battle from Humphrey and Wallace, you have disproven the doubters and redeemed your name. Your lead dwindled a bit as Wallace’s appeal dampened, but your coalition managed to remain intact.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/ending/s0.l100.c32/text: Congratulations! Despite the intense battle from Humphrey and Wallace, you have disproven the doubters and redeemed your name. The bombing halt and Wallace collapsing in the north nearly lost you the election, but you managed to hang on.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/ending/s0.l103.c33/text: For the first time since 1888, the winner of the electoral vote lost the popular vote. It seems many people underestimated how much of an effect Wallace had on your campaign in the south.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/ending/s0.l106.c27/text: After your second loss in a presidential election, your chances of being renominated for the presidency, or ANYTHING for that matter is nearly zero. Retirement and an elder statesman position are all that will await you. It seems Americans will once and for all not have Nixon to kick around…
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/ending/s0.l108.c32/text: Despite the environment seemingly being perfect for a Nixon comeback, you had a sudden and shocking reversal of fortunes, and have lost yet another presidential election. Republicans are shocked they have now lost 7 of the last 9 presidential elections. With the margins being as close as 8 years ago, you are already having flashbacks of 1960.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/ending/s0.l111.c32/text: Despite the environment seemingly being perfect for a Nixon comeback, you had a sudden and shocking reversal of fortunes, and have lost yet another presidential election. Republicans are shocked they have now lost 8 of the last 10 presidential elections. Somehow you managed to do worse compared to 1960. Nobody is quite sure how that is even possible, but suffice it to say you will receive much of the blame.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/ending/s0.l113.c32/text: Despite the environment seemingly being perfect for a Nixon comeback, you had a sudden and shocking reversal of fortunes, and have lost yet another presidential election. Republicans are shocked they have now lost 8 of the last 10 presidential elections. Not only did you lose, but you got crushed. Under the weight of two ideologically different candidates, your moderate positions seemed to not appeal. If the skirmish between liberal and conservative republicans wasn’t already bad, it was going to get a lot worse after this.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/ending/s0.l117.c33/text: At the end of the day, in possibly the most shocking turn of events, the popular vote fell in your favour. Nobody is sure what to make of this, but maybe the Democrats can use their house and senate supermajorities, combined with disaffected Republicans, to pass electoral reform?
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/ending/s0.l122.c27/text: A return to the Senate might be in order, so you might defend liberalism from demise during Nixon's administration, or gearing up for a run in 1972. perhaps you can do both. In any case, let's hope Nixon can cool tensions in America and bring the troops home.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/ending/s0.l124.c32/text: Despite your best efforts in a tough climate, Richard Nixon will succeed Johnson in the presidency. It was always going to be difficult being so closely associated with an unpopular administration, in a divided party. You still fought hard, and took Nixon to the brink as Kennedy did in 60.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/ending/s0.l126.c32/text: Despite your best efforts in a tough climate, Richard Nixon will succeed Johnson in the presidency. It was always going to be difficult being so closely associated with an unpopular administration, in a divided party. The crime and rioting took a toll on your campaign hard, and Nixon's law and order theme really hit home for many Americans.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/ending/s0.l128.c32/text: Despite your best efforts in a tough climate, Richard Nixon will succeed Johnson in the presidency. It was always going to be difficult being so closely associated with an unpopular administration, in a divided party. It seems liberalism very well might be over with this loss, as you have been crushed. A more moderate candidate in 4 years will likely be chosen.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/ending/s0.l131.c27/text: Your first course of action is to fix what Johnson caused. Vietnam and the riots need to be dealt with. Johnson might not like how you deal with it, but this is your administration, and you'll deal with it the way you do. Act quickly, or you just might become as unpopular as Johnson.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/ending/s0.l133.c32/text: The happy warrior rises! Despite a climate of chaos and a split in the Democratic Party, you've beaten back the opposition and secured a third term for the Democrats. Johnson breathes a sigh of relief after this, and poor Nixon is once again a loser. To the shock of pundits countrywide, you beat Nixon and Wallace handily. The bombing halt and your inspiring words compared to Nixon must have won it for you.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/ending/s0.l135.c32/text: The happy warrior rises! Despite a climate of chaos and a split in the Democratic Party, you've beaten back the opposition and secured a third term for the Democrats. Johnson breathes a sigh of relief after this, and poor Nixon is once again a loser. It seems America is ready to give the New Deal Democrats one last chance. If you succeed, you might be able to rebuild the coalition that's won them so many elections (well, not the Deep South, but you knew that).
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/ending/s0.l137.c32/text: The happy warrior rises! Despite a climate of chaos and a split in the Democratic Party, you've beaten back the opposition and secured a third term for the Democrats. Johnson breathes a sigh of relief after this, and poor Nixon is once again a loser. He did quite well, however, so you best work hard, lest the midterms act mercilessly.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/ending/s0.l141.c23/text: As expected, you lost the 1968 election
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/ending/s0.l142.c23/text: What happens next is your choice. Another governorship wouldn't hurt, and perhaps you can run again in 4 years if you're up to it. Unfortunately (for you), civil rights will persist.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/ending/s0.l148.c32/text: In a shock to all parties involved, neither Hubert Horatio Humphrey nor Richard Milhous Nixon will be the next president of the United States. Somehow, you managed to come out on top. Southerners are ecstatic, liberals are foaming at the mouth, and the black population has never been more fearful.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/ending/s0.l149.c31/text: Pundits are shocked, trying to figure out how you managed to capture states outside the deep south to win it all. What happens next is entirely unknown. Its likely a crusader against the civil rights bill will happen, as well as the deconstruction of Great Society, and the escalation of Vietnam. Whatever happens, sit back and relax knowing you've done the greatest upset in US political history!
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/ending/s0.l152.c32/text: As most expected, you've lost. This isn't a surprise, as you're a third party. even worse, your second goal of deadlocking the electoral college failed. You did, however, come very close, picking up a number of states you weren't expected to pick up. It seems that your crusade for the south turned out really well. You could run in four years perhaps, and try and win the same coalition, trying to deadlock the election then. You've sent a clear message to the Democrats; the south isn't to be ignored,
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/ending/s0.l154.c32/text: As most expected, you've lost. This isn't a surprise, as you're a third party. even worse, your second goal of deadlocking the electoral college failed. You did, however, poll a bit higher above what you were set to win. So good job outdoing your predictions. The south isn't done yet, as you've shown here.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/ending/s0.l156.c32/text: As most expected, you've lost. This isn't a surprise, as you're a third party. even worse, your second goal of deadlocking the electoral college failed. You won just about as much as expected, and yet it wasn't enough. Your supporters are disillusioned that you weren't able to deadlock the college. That's how it is, though...
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/questions_json/321@0/de: What will be the overall theme of your campaign as you criss-cross the United States?
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/questions_json/322@1/de: What will be the thrust of your speech as you accept the Republican nomination in Miami?
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/questions_json/338@2/de: What is more important for your campaign -- competing with Humphrey in the swing states, or winning over Wallace voters in the south?
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/questions_json/256@3/de: Are you satisfied with the progress of desegregation in this country since the passage of the Civil Rights Act of 1964?
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/questions_json/326@4/de: Your Democratic counterpart has repeatedly challenged you to a debate. After your debacle against Kennedy in 1960, will you debate your opponent this time?
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/questions_json/255@5/de: Are you satisfied with this nation's economic performance over the previous five years?
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/questions_json/254@6/de: What is your opinion of Lyndon Johnson's new Medicare program?
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/questions_json/257@7/de: Would you be willing to call an unconditional bombing halt of North Vietnam in the hopes of restarting peace negotiations?
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/questions_json/285@8/de: Do you support the Child Nutrition Act of 1966, which provides free breakfast and milk to qualified schoolchildren of impoverished backgrounds? Or do you believe that the program is too costly and constitutes a misuse of federal power?
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/questions_json/290@9/de: The unemployment rate is currently under 4%, in spite of the chaos that prevails in our nation. What will you do as president to keep unemployment low?
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/questions_json/287@10/d: How would you prevent campus incidents like the takeover of Columbia University that occurred this past spring?
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/questions_json/260@11/d: What do you think about the efforts of the AFL-CIO and other large unions? Do they have a positive effect on America?
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/questions_json/329@12/d: An alarming percentage of voters are inspired by the aggressively racist rhetoric of George Wallace. What will you do to win this group?
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/questions_json/323@13/d: How far are you willing to go to compete in the American South against the campaign of George Wallace?
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/questions_json/280@14/d: What is your opinion of the Immigration and Nationality Act of 1965? Is it a good idea to liberalize our immigration policy and to outlaw national origin quotas?
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/questions_json/324@15/d: As Governor of California, Ronald Reagan will be crucial to your chances in that state. Can you reassure him that you are sufficiently conservative to warrant his enthusiasm after your battle for the Republican nomination?
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/questions_json/286@16/d: Can we all agree that the Black Panthers are a menace to the security of the United States?
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/questions_json/277@17/d: Do you think the Department of Housing and Urban Development, newly created by Lyndon Johnson, serves a useful purpose in American life?
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/questions_json/258@18/d: Would you consider sending troops into Laos, Cambodia, or North Vietnam to more aggressively combat the flow of Communist troops into South Vietnam?
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/questions_json/291@19/d: Do you believe that President Johnson overstepped his bounds in negotiating the Kennedy Round of trade agreements? Do you support the liberalization of international trade under the GATT?
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/questions_json/281@20/d: What is causing the massive increase of crime in America? How will you reverse the trend?
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/questions_json/269@21/d: What is your stance on the Six-Day War that occurred last year, and how should Israel handle the new territories it has taken possession of?
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/questions_json/270@22/d: Are you concerned with some of the activist stances that Earl Warren has taken in his time with the Supreme Court?
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/questions_json/292@23/d: Do we need more spending in the War on Poverty, especially in light of the riots since 1965?
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/questions_json/325@24/d: Sources have indicated that Johnson is close to reaching a breakthrough in negotiations with the North Vietnamese, which could almost assure a Democratic win on Tuesday. An operative with connections to the South Vietnam government is willing to sabotage these negotiations with promises that you will offer a better deal when elected. Will you take a chance on this plan?
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/1679@0/des: Absolutely not. I'm looking for ways to end this war with an honorable peace agreement, not ways to incite the wrath of Red China.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/1680@1/des: We need to pull our forces out of Vietnam as soon as possible. This war is a national disgrace.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/1661@2/des: Medicare is the first step towards socialized medicine in this country. We need to end this program as soon as possible and return health care to the states and to the people.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/1662@3/des: We need to be very cautious about this program. It's important to ensure that the indigent can receive care, but programs like these always run the risk of adding precipitously to our national deficit.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/1663@4/des: I commend this piece of legislation. Already we see many Americans receiving health care who would otherwise be stricken with serious and/or fatal conditions.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/1664@5/des: Medicare is only the beginning of what we need to do in this country. I support a national health care system for all Americans.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/1665@6/des: How can anyone be satisfied with the course our nation has taken? Inflation is killing the value of the dollar and the gold standard itself is at risk. Unemployment is highest under the Johnson Administration among the very people he claims to care about the most.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/1666@7/des: Our current economic path is not sustainable. We need to continue the growth we have seen but we cannot allow this inflation we have to continue.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/1667@8/des: The unemployment rate right now is under four percent. Workers, particularly those in labor unions, enjoy high purchasing power and an ever-expanding lifestyle. Economic growth throughout the 1960s has been outstanding.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/1668@9/des: The worst thing we can do right now is to sabotage the progress we have seen by continuing to squander our money on a war in Vietnam. I support a full employment economy as well -- meaning we must be vigilant against misguided attempts to raise interest rates.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/1669@10/de: Whites and Negroes are naturally unsuited to mix together in society. The entire premise of desegregation is a farce, and my campaign is dedicated to ending this misguided policy.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/1670@11/de: I strongly support what we have done to end the insidious practice of segregation in the South. However I'm also alarmed at some of the ideas I've heard about forced integration of neighborhoods, or the proposed busing of students to distant schools.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/1671@12/de: We have achieved great strides on this issue in the past twenty years -- and let the record show that I shepherd the Civil Rights Act of 1957 through the Senate and have supported Civil Rights bills during my time in the House and Senate. We still have a long way to go, however, before we can truly realize the dream of Martin Luther King.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/1672@13/de: We need to be very aggressive in fighting racism and its effects where they exist. I support programs such as busing, affirmative action, the new HUD department, and anything else that is necessary to integrate all regions of the United States.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/1673@14/de: If anything, we need to escalate the bombing of North Vietnam. I don't go to bed at night with the feeling that they truly respect the power of America.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/1674@15/de: We will never win the peace in Vietnam by caving in to the Communists. I cannot support such an ill-conceived measure.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/1675@16/de: I would be willing to take this step and see what develops. It is imperative that we end the war in Vietnam as soon as possible.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/1676@17/de: We need to pull our forces out of Vietnam as soon as possible. This war is a national disgrace.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/1677@18/de: I can't believe we haven't done this yet. How on earth are we supposed to win a war against an insidious enemy with one hand tied behind our back?
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/1678@19/de: I don't think that kind of escalation is wise. The last thing we need is a regional war. I would stick to our mission of defending South Vietnam and preventing the spread of Communism.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/1685@20/de: We should always be wary of the corruption inherent in these large unions. I cannot say that I'm a supporter of the AFL-CIO.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/1686@21/de: Every man should have a choice on whether to join a union or not. These large outfits monopolize the work force and use their power to perpetrate voter fraud and to enrich their bosses.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/1687@22/de: The AFL-CIO is a centerpiece of the great American bargain. Our economy can never thrive unless the people who work to keep it going thrive as well. I fully support the AFL-CIO.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/1716@23/de: Israel has every right to these territories they now occupy. They were attacked from all sides by an enemy bent on their destruction.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/1717@24/de: As President, I'm confident that all sides can come together and negotiate a long-term peace agreement. Certainly the return of the Sinai or the Golan Heights should not be off the table.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/1718@25/de: I fully support Israel's right to defend herself. However, I believe that these territories should be returned to the Arab states as a first step towards peace negotiations.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/1719@26/de: This business in Israel is no business of America. I wish them the best, but we should not be obtrusively inserting ourselves into these multilateral peace negotiations. Doing so will only serve to entangle us in the long run.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/1720@27/de: Earl Warren is without a doubt the worst Supreme Court justice in the history of the United States. From Brown v. Board of Education up through the present day, he has been nothing but an agent of tyranny for the federal government.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/1721@28/de: On the balance I would not appoint another justice like Mr. Warren. Desegregating our schools was one thing, but he has gone off the deep end on these issues like school prayer, Miranda rights, and other activist decisions.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/1722@29/de: It would be better in some cases if we could get Congress to make these decisions, but I do support the stances Mr. Warren has taken on the Court.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/1723@30/de: The Warren Court is the first Supreme Court in history which has had the guts to use constitutional law for the benefit of the common citizen. I will continue to appoint sound judges like Mr. Warren, Abe Fortas, and Thurgood Marshall.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/1745@31/de: Can we just clarify my position on all of these fancy programs Johnson created? I oppose all of them. That includes HUD which will infringe on the rights of property owners and increase crime in our working class neighborhoods.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/1746@32/de: I will do my best to ensure that this program is managed soundly and does not become some kind of welfare program without accountability.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/1747@33/de: We need to do everything in our power to ensure that our poorest citizens have affordable housing. The HUD department is a centerpiece of this initiative.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/1756@34/de: The Negro problem apparently wasn't enough for our federal bureaucrats, because they decided to add Mexicans and Orientals to the list as well. I oppose new immigration to this country.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/1757@35/de: We need to be vigilant on the amount of immigration that we allow, but I also agree that we shouldn't restrict the practice based on national origin. In a Cold War world, we need to be mindful of international perceptions.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/1758@36/de: This is a fair and sensible policy that will allow skilled immigrants to enter the United States. It's ludicrous to state that this will somehow compromise our culture and our values.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/1759@37/de: Our former immigration policy was a national embarrassment. This country was built by immigrants and my only complaint right now is that the overall number of visas is still far too low for our needs.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/1760@38/de: This increase in crime we see is the natural consequence of integration. I will not allow the black community in this country to get fancified notions of what they can get away with when I'm President.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/1761@39/de: We have a system in place that gives precedence to the rights of criminals over law-abiding citizens. I will take a firm stand on this issue as President.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/1762@40/de: We need to improve our policing practices, prevent riots and disorder, and also address the underlying economic causes that spread dissatisfaction with the status quo.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/1763@41/de: There is a cynicism in our poorest neighborhoods engendered by poverty and by the brutality of the police. I will vigorously address both of these issues when I'm elected.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/1774@42/de: I don't think anyone opposes the idea of providing milk to our poor kids. My contention, however, is that the state and local governments are more in tune with their needs than some bureaucrats in Washington.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/1775@43/de: This is a sensible piece of legislation. I support it and I think that every decent American supports it too.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/1776@44/de: The Black Panthers are a radical group of militants who are plotting the overthrow of the United States government. It is my firm position, in accordance with the Constitution, that anyone planning treason against our country should be imprisoned and possibly executed.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/1777@45/de: I support a fair shake for every American. I support programs that help black businesses. I support desegregation. I oppose groups like the Black Panthers that have contributed to the rioting and chaos that has swept the nation these past three years.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/1778@46/de: Our goal is a society that works for everyone. The Black Panthers have instigated some ugly incidents, and I believe on the balance that they have done more harm than good for the cause of integration.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/1779@47/de: How these students have not been expelled is beyond me. If Administrators want to be complicit in the degradation of a private university, that is their own business. However, I won't spend a dime of federal money on a school that coddles radical agitators.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/1780@48/de: I will crack down on dope-smoking, homosexuality, LSD binging, illegal protesting, and flag-burning. These practices are the tools of left-wingers and Communists who wish to undermine our society.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/1781@49/de: There are some legitimate complaints behind these abhorrent actions. I will work for peace in Vietnam and civil rights in the United States. In the meantime, I support the rights of university administrators as they combat this problem.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/1788@50/de: The unemployment rate won't stay low for long if we continue to pass new regulations on housing, mining, and industrial concerns. I speak for the working man when I say that we need to get the federal government out of these areas.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/1789@51/de: We are keeping the unemployment rate artificially depressed with unsound fiscal and monetary policies. In the long-run, this will lead to a poor economy and higher unemployment.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/1790@52/de: Democratic management of the economy these past eight years has been a clear success. I will continue to protect our unions and support the economy with smart government action.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/1791@53/de: There is far more we can do. Jobs training programs and a continued fight against discrimination will ensure that all Americans can share in the low unemployment rate.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/1792@54/de: International trade will undermine the prosperity of the working man as quickly as it will undermine the sovereignty of the United States. I don't support any of these global organizations.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/1793@55/de: I support the overall thrust of this policy. Foreign trade supports our Cold War allies, reduces the cost of goods in America, and supports a broader economic prosperity.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/1794@56/de: I support these international trade negotiations, but we must be sure that we don't undermine the rights of our own unions with one-sided agreements.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/1795@57/de: The War on Poverty is a national disgrace. It is a program that steals from the productive to finance the lazy and the shiftless.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/1796@58/de: We need to focus less on handouts and more on encouraging initiative among our black and ethnic business owners. They will build the prosperity in our inner cities. I will analyze the War on Poverty on a program-by-program basis and cut those which are unnecessary.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/1797@59/de: I support the War on Poverty as it stands. We have passed a lot of new initiatives and we should wait to see what effect they have. To me, cracking down on the law and order issues is more important.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/1798@60/de: We are the greatest nation on earth and we cannot rest until every citizen has an opportunity to share in that prosperity.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/3227@61/de: I am the true conservative in this election. I support free enterprise, a hard line against Communism, and a devolution of responsibilities to the state governments.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/3228@62/de: My primary focus is to return law and order to this country. The riots, the murders, the drug use, and the protests we've seen since 1965 are unacceptable.
en.1968_Nixon_Agnew/answers_json/3229@63/de: Lyndon Johnson has created more programs and agencies than any President except for FDR. I will act more in line with the wishes of the American people.

理查德·尼克松听着法官喋喋不休，闭上眼睛，等着这句话结束。审判的压力让他整夜难以入睡，不知不觉，他就失去了意识。突然，法官的叫喊把他惊醒了：“尼克松！你作何答辩？……”

“对于在法庭上睡觉这一项罪名呢？……”

“你什么时候说了这——其实，是的，法官大人。自由派媒体一直在歪曲我的形象。我只是在闭目养神。”

今天，我站在亚伯拉罕·林肯曾经站过的地方，向我的国家庄严宣誓。因此，从这座美国的堡垒，从那些为这个国家奠定自由原则的伟人精神所系之地，再次擂响自由的战鼓，正是理所应当——正如我们的先辈一代又一代，在历史上无数次做过的那样。让我们响应血液中热爱自由的召唤，向那把锁链铐在黑人身上的暴政作出回答。以这个世界上最伟大的国家之名，我在尘土中划下界线，把挑战的铁手套掷到暴政脚下……我要说……今天废除种族隔离……明天废除种族隔离……永远废除种族隔离！
